key_insight: SympFormer derives accelerated attention blocks from inertial, damped Hamiltonian dynamics on spaces of probability measures.
engineering_relevance: The framework motivates geometry-aware token and momentum updates that improve next-token prediction over momentum-only controls in the reported experiments.
method: Develop local-mobility geometry for Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, plus quotient Stein geometry for linear attention.
Establish domains for gradient-flow and Hamiltonian formulations, and characterize global existence versus moment blow-up for linear attention.
Link continuous moment blow-up to discrete token-norm threshold depth and introduce geometric update corrections.
evidence_signal: Decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText report lower validation negative log-likelihood with geometric corrections than with momentum-only controls.
watch_item: The theory identifies domain restrictions and possible finite-time moment blow-up; the abstract does not establish benefits at large-model scale.
paper_title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
